Task-oriented wording helps recognition; replace incorrect 71/10 counts with candidate 88/11 and measure actual lengths separately.
Adopt clearer consistent action/object labels. Do not infer that overlapping words mean interchangeable contracts or universal memory failure.
Regroup into four packs, retain distinguishing domain words, and remove catch-all plugin ambiguity. The list contains 11 packs, not 10.
Profiles and specialist reviews remain useful standalone capabilities; routing fixtures are not evidence that their existence causes errors.
Do not collapse specialists into orchestrators. Explicit-only loading costs are client-dependent; no universal zero-cost claim.
Fresh-context review remains optional and authorized. Self-review remains useful; isolation is not correctness.

Add comprehension and plan/code routes using existing capabilities. Investigate failed reads and reviewer error as well as document gaps.
Evidence-based rejection and repair already exist; preserve dispositions and permit reopening on new evidence.

Fixture counts and compiler evidence do not establish comparative behavioral quality.
Action/object names and four packs adopted; reject arbitrary 20-character limit and domain-word removal.

One-to-one map retains alignment, framing and test planning/execution separately; proposed alternate spellings superseded by approved map.
Keep review, reviewer request, consolidation, data authority, public boundary and security contracts separate.
Rename research, claims, governance, publication and diagnosis without merging different permissions or contracts.

Retain explicit evidence scope, candidate identity and qualifications; dated source inspection is not installed behavior.
Separate navigation quality from catalog breadth and different EGM responsibilities.
Recognizable labels matter; format compliance alone does not make names usable. Preserve improved descriptions.
User selected full canonical migration rather than labels first; retain useful display wording.
Separate identifiers, labels, descriptions, pack membership and task entry points; preserve invocation controls.
